By this common order, W.P. No.24260/2023 and W.P. No. 31001/2023 shall be decided.
2. For the sake of convenience, facts of W.P. No.24260/2023 shall be considered.

3. This petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed seeking following relief(s):-
I. 1.

To issue a writ in the nature of certiorari to quashing the entire proceedings for acquisition started vide order dt. 09.03.2018 and also impugned order dated 16.03.2022 (Annexure P/1) passed by Respondent No.4, in the interest of justice.

sentences.text: III. 3.
To summon the entire relevant record from the possession of the Respondents Department for kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court.
IV. 4.
To issue a writ in the nature of mandamus directing the Resopndent no.7 to provide continuous electricity to the petitioners till they are properly resettled and adequately compensated as per law.
V. Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper may kindly be granted.
4. The facts of the case which are necessary for disposal of this petition in short are that the petitioners have their agricultural lands situated in village Khamra and Jogipura, District Sagar.
Petitioner No.1 is having 8 acres of land in village Khamra and 8 acres of land in village Jogipura.
Petitioner No.2 is having 8 acres of land in village Jogipura.
Petitioner No.3 is having 9 acres of land in village Jogipura.
Petitioner No.4 is having 8 acres of land in village Jogipura.
Petitioner No.5 is having 15 acres of land in village Khamra.
Petitioner No.6 is having 24 acres of land in village Khamra.
Petitioner No.7 is having 5 acres of land in village Khamra.
Petitioner No.8 is having 8.5 acres of land in village Khamra and petitioner No.9 is having 9 acres of land in village Khamra.

5. It is the case of petitioners that apart from their agricultural lands, they are also having their dwelling houses in village Khamra/ Jogipura along with Well, small gardens, fruit trees and vegetable plants.
They were to be relocated in the light of Nauradehi National Park.

It is the case of petitioners that in place of acquiring their lands as per the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short 'Act,
2013'), they are being coerced to accept lump sum payment of Rs.15,00,000/- as a total compensation including resettlement and rehabilitation package.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Since none of the petitioners had accepted the money, and therefore, an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- has been transferred to their account and they have been asked to utilize the money so that remaining amount of Rs.14,00,000/-
can also be transferred.

6. Being aggrieved by the high-handed action of the respondents, petitioners represented to SDO Deori, SDO Forest, Collector Sagar as well as to Commissioner, Sagar Division Sagar but they could not get any respite.

7. It is submitted that to forcefully evict the petitioners, respondents have disconnected their electricity connection in spite of the fact that none of the petitioners are in arrears of any electricity bills.

Thus, it is submitted that the respondents are forcibly acquiring the land and therefore, giving a petty amount of Rs.15,00,000/- by way of compensation including resettlement and rehabilitation package is insufficient and the said proposal was not accepted by the petitioners but by exercising Lachhaman Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129887568/
2 undue influence, respondents are threatening the petitioners.
8.

sentences.text: Per contra, petition is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State.
It is submitted that the National Tiger Conservation Authority of India has issued relocation packages of core/crit habit adopted in the Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy, 2007.

entities.text: National Tiger Conservation Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, the Ministry of Environment & Forests, National Conservation Authority of India issued certain instructions with regard to compensation for the implementation of centrally sponsored scheme of the Project Tiger.
Accordingly, the State of Madhya Pradesh vide letter dated 31/03/2008 and 30/10/2008 had also issued certain instructions for implementation of centrally sponsored scheme of the Project Tiger.
A Resolution dated 17/08/2019 was passed by the Members of Gram Sabha Khamrapathar and they agreed for rehabilitation and resettlement on payment of compensation of Rupees Ten Lakhs.
Accordingly, petitioners submitted their consents and details of the family members along with other documents.

The Collector constituted a Committee for valuation of immovable property of the villagers and thereafter Sub Divisional Level Committee after taking into consideration the report,
prepared a list of eligible villagers for rehabilitation package.
Individual objections raised by the villagers have been decided by the District Level Rehabilitation Committee Sagar.

The Collector,
Sagar vide order dated 14/10/2022 sanctioned the compensation for payment to the villagers of village Khamrapathar and Jogipathar Tahsil Deori, District Sagar, wherein the names of the petitioners find place and accordingly, amount of Rs.15,00,000/- was transferred in their bank accounts.

It is submitted that the entire exercise has been carried out by the respondents in pursuant to the instructions issued by Government of India, Ministry of Environment & Forest,
National Tiger Conservation Authority as well as Forest Department of State of Madhya Pradesh.

entities.text: Forest Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Gram Sabha of village Khamrapathar has already passed the Resolution thereby accepting the Scheme for Rehabilitation & Resettlement of villages and accordingly, petitioners also submitted their consents.
It is submitted that once the petitioners themselves have accepted the compensation offered by the respondents, therefore now they cannot take a turn around to claim coercion.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
10.
Undisputedly, the State is in a dominating position.

It is the case of respondents that the compensation has been paid in accordance with the instructions issued by Government of India,
Ministry of Environment & Forest, National Tiger Conservation Authority as well the State of Madhya Pradesh.
Whereas, it is the case of petitioners that they had never given any consent and their consents have been obtained by coercion.
11. Therefore, the only question for consideration is as to whether the Policy framed by the respondents and the amount of compensation awarded to the persons is proper and conscionable?

12. Section 16 of Indian Contract Act, 1872 reads as under:-
"16. 'Undue influence' defined.- (1) A contract is said to be induced by 'undue influence' where the relations subsisting between the parties are such that one of the parties is in a position to dominate the will of the other and uses that position to obtain an unfair advantage over the other.

Lachhaman Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129887568/
3

entities.text: Lachhaman Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing principle, a person is deemed to be in a position to dominate the will of another- (a) where he holds a real or apparent authority over the other, or where he stands in a fiduciary relation to the other; or (b) where he makes a contract with a person whose mental capacity is temporarily or permanently affected by reason of age, illness, or mental or bodily distress.

(3) Where a person who is in a position to dominate the will of another, enters into a contract with him, and the transaction appears, on the face of it or on the evidence adduced, to be unconscionable, the burden of proving that such contract was not induced by undue influence shall lie upon the person in a position to dominate the will of the other.

Nothing in this sub-section shall affect the provisions of section 111 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (1 of 1872)."
13.
Thus, it is clear that 'undue influence' means that one of the parties is in a position to dominate the will of the other and uses that position to obtain an unfair advantage over the other.

Further, if the transaction appears to be unconscionable, the burden of proving that such contract was not induced by undue influence shall be upon the person in a position to dominate the will of the other.

14. Now the first question for consideration is as to whether the contract in question is unconscionable or not?
15.
Respondents have filed copy of some of the proceedings in respect of various persons.

As per Annexure-R/4, Kanai is the owner of 2.85 hectares of land apart from house, Well etc; Daulat is the owner of 2.51 hectares of land apart from house, Well etc; Preetam is the owner of 3.10 hectares of land apart from house, Well etc; Manmod is the owner of 3.40 hectares of land apart from house,
Well etc; Pooran is the owner of 4.57 hectares of land apart from house, Well etc; Kadori is the owner of 9.20 hectares of land apart from house, Well etc; Parasram is the owner of 3.32 hectares of land apart from house, Well etc; Parshottam is the owner of 6.94 hectares of land apart from house,
Well etc, but all of them have been paid Rs.15,00,000/- by way of full and final compensation.
16.

How a person who is the owner of 9.20 hectares of land apart from house, trees, well etc. is entitled for Rs.15,00,000/- only specifically when same amount has been paid to the other persons who are having less or no land at all?

17. Accordingly, counsel for respondents was directed to justify the stand of the respondents that by making payment of Rs.15,00,000/-, they have adequately compensated the persons who are liable to be uprooted.

sentences.text: However, except by referring to the instructions already referred, counsel for the State could not justify that how an owner of more land is entitled for the same amount which is paid to the person having less land or no land at all.
19. Thus, it is clear that the act of respondents is unconscionable.
Therefore, the burden is on the respondents to show that they have not induced the petitioners by applying undue influence.
20. Every petitioner is merely a villager and they cannot resist against the might of the State.
Even according to the petitioners, electricity connection has been disconnected to compel them to vacate their lands.

21. In a similar situation, this Court in the case of Manoj Kumar Prajapati and Others Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh and Others decided on 19/01/2024 in Writ Petition No.19418/2017 has held as under:-
"24.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, it is clear that without there being any statutory provision of law,
respondents unilaterally issued executive instructions and on the basis of the same,
the consent letters were obtained and amount has been deposited in the accounts of petitioners.

Since respondents have miserably failed in discharging their duty as required under Section 16 (3) of Contract Act therefore, this Court is left with no other option but to accept the contention of counsel for petitioners that consent letters were obtained under undue influence."
22.
Thus, it is held that the consent letters which were obtained from petitioners were obtained under undue influence, therefore, they are quashed.
23. Now the next question for consideration is that what should be the proper mode for acquisition of land.

24. Section 24 of Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 reads as under:-
"24. Acquisition of rights.- (1) In the case of a claim to a right in or over any land referred to in section 19, the Collector shall pass an order admitting or rejecting the same in whole or in part.
(2) If such claim is admitted in whole or in part, the Collector may either- (a) exclude such land from the limits of the proposed sanctuary; or (b) proceed to acquire such land or rights, except where by an agreement between the owner of such land or holder of rights and the Government, the owner or holder of such rights has agreed to surrender his rights to the Government, in or over such land, and on payment of such compensation, as is provided in the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Lachhaman Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129887568/
5 Resettlement Act, 2013 (30 of 2013);
(c) allow, in consultation with the Chief Wild Life Warden, the continuation of any right of any person in or over any land within the limits of the sanctuary."
25.

Since the respondents have failed to prove that the proceedings done by them were conscionable and were not the outcome of undue influence, therefore, it is held that all agreements obtained from the petitioners are voidable at the instance of the petitioners in the light of Section 19 of Contract Act.

26. In the light of Section 24(2) of Wild Life (Protection) Act, it is clear that if any person is having a land comprised within the limits of sanctuary, then the Collector has to proceed as per the provisions Section 24(2) of Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
The Collector has to acquire the land as per the provisions of Act, 2013.

27. Therefore, it is directed that in case if the petitioner(s) refund the amount of Rs.15,00,000/-
(Rupees Fifteen Lakhs) which has already been deposited in their accounts and makes an application for acquisition of land as per the provisions of Act, 2013
, then the Competent Authority shall initiate proceedings under the Act, 2013 and shall assess the compensation under the provisions of Act, 2013.

28. In case the amount is not refunded and an application for acquisition as per Act, 2013 is not filed within a period of three months from today, then this order shall automatically lose its effect.
29. With aforesaid observations, petition(s) is/ are finally disposed of.
